## Stagger siblings

[`MoveStaggerDirective`](/docs/reference/move-stagger-directive) is a context provider: it gives each child's `moveEnter`, `moveInView` or variant a delay computed from its position in the DOM, so it works with `@for` without any manual index bookkeeping. Step accepts a number (milliseconds) or a string with a unit.

:::code features.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-features',
  imports: [MoveStaggerDirective, MoveEnterDirective],
  template: `
    <ul moveStagger moveStaggerStep="80ms">
      @for (item of items; track item) {
        <li moveEnter="fade-up">{{ item }}</li>
      }
    </ul>
  `,
})
export class Features {
  protected readonly items = ['Fast', 'Accessible', 'Typed'];
}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/stagger-and-scroll.ts#L11-L24)

`moveStaggerDirection` orders the delays from the `first` child, the `last`, or the `center`.

::playground[stagger]

The children use `moveEnter`, which is one-shot, so the playground recreates the list when a setting changes. [Open the full stagger playground](/demos/stagger).

Combine it with `moveInView` to reveal sections one after another as they scroll into view:

:::code sections.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-sections',
  imports: [MoveStaggerDirective, MoveInViewDirective],
  template: `
    <section moveStagger moveStaggerStep="100ms">
      <article moveInView="fade-up">One</article>
      <article moveInView="fade-up">Two</article>
      <article moveInView="fade-up">Three</article>
    </section>
  `,
})
export class Sections {}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/stagger-and-scroll.ts#L28-L39)

## Scroll-linked motion

[`MoveScrollDirective`](/docs/reference/move-scroll-directive) maps scroll progress onto an animation: progress `0` to `1` becomes the timeline from start to end, and the directive exposes `progress` as a signal. [`MoveParallaxDirective`](/docs/reference/move-parallax-directive) does the same with an automatically computed translate range.

:::code scroll-hero.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-scroll-hero',
  imports: [MoveScrollDirective],
  template: `
    <!-- Duration is always 1000ms linear internally: scroll progress maps 1:1 onto the timeline. -->
    <div [moveScroll]="{ y: [0, 120], opacity: [1, 0.2] }" #hero="moveScroll">
      Progress: {{ hero.progress() }}
    </div>
  `,
})
export class ScrollHero {}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/stagger-and-scroll.ts#L43-L53)

Both read the native scroll position (smoothed with a short interpolation) and fall back to the end state under reduced motion. Point `moveScrollContainer` or `moveParallaxContainer` at a selector for an inner scroll container.

> [!NOTE]
> Native scrolling is the default everywhere on this site. `moveSmoothScroll` and `SmoothScrollService` change how wheel and touch scrolling feel and are **experimental**; prefer native scrolling.

## Loops

[`MoveLoopDirective`](/docs/reference/move-loop-directive) repeats a preset or keyframes. Use it for short, meaningful loops (a spinner, a subtle pulse) and keep them `aria-hidden` when decorative. Loops stop under reduced motion.

:::code spinner.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-spinner',
  imports: [MoveLoopDirective],
  template: `<span moveLoop="spin" moveDuration="1s" aria-hidden="true">◐</span>`,
})
export class Spinner {}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/stagger-and-scroll.ts#L57-L62)
